text:
mike_support: customer on enterprise tier reports /v1/generate (mode=json) failing with a JSON.parse error when their prompt contains file paths. they pasted the client error: "JSON.parse error: Unexpected token \ in JSON at position 145"

sara_support: can you paste the request_id and the exact payload they sent? also did they see a 4xx or a 5xx?

mike_support: request_id=req_8a2c7f. Customer says server returned 400. here's the payload they used (redacted):
```json
{
  "mode": "json",
  "input": [
    {"type": "file", "path": "C:\Users\alice\docs\report.pdf"},
    {"type": "note", "text": "see attached"}
  ]
}
```

sara_support: thanks. that payload looks fine client-side (they escape backslashes). are we doing any additional escaping on the server or inside the structured-output serializer? @ben_prod any ideas?

ben_prod: looking at logs for req_8a2c7f — our generator returned a structured JSON chunk that ended up with a raw unescaped backslash sequence when concatenated across stream boundaries. snippet from our post-assembly log: `{"items":[{"path":"C:\Users\alice\docs\report.pdf"},` then later the rest got appended as `\notes"}]}` and the final blob became invalid: `{"items":[{"path":"C:\Users\alice\docseport.pdf"},` which breaks JSON.parse on the client.

tom_eng: this smells like double-encoding + chunked streaming boundary issue. when we re-serialize tokens into the structured mode stream we escape once, then the stream join performs another escape pass in some codepath. we should be careful to only escape at the final render pass.

mike_support: customer also mentioned they saw a billing spike because their client retried 5x after the 400, so this caused extra charges. billing_team: any quick mitigation we can offer while we patch?

billing_team: we can issue a one-time credit for the retries once support confirms timestamps & request ids. please collect req_8a2c7f and a short timeline. we can do that ASAP. :+1:

ben_prod: repro steps I used locally: curl to /v1/generate with mode=json and an input array containing a Windows path. server streamed back structured chunks; if you interrupt or if buffering reflows chunks, the escaping can be split. minimal repro:
```bash
curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"mode":"json","input":[{"type":"file","path":"C:\Users\alice\docs\report.pdf"}]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | sed -n '1,200p'
```

ben_prod: observed final concatenated output (invalid):
```json
{"items":[{"path":"C:\Users\alice\docs\report.pdf"}, {"note":"line1\nline2"},
```
(note missing closing brackets because a split escape produced a parse error)

tom_eng: proposed fix: stop double-escaping at stream assembly boundary, add a unit test that simulates chunk reflow with backslashes and quotes, and add a canary deploy to dedicated for 24h. i'll open a PR for the serializer fix.

sara_support: i'll reply to customer with an interim workaround: ask them to base64-encode file paths in the JSON payload (we'll accept encoded strings), or ask them to escape again as a temporary measure. also promise a credit and update once we ship the fix.

mike_support: customer ok with base64 workaround for now. tracking note: escalate to eng-runtime, tag PR to change log and include regression test. @tom_eng please include the request_id in the fix branch so we can correlate.

infra-bot: deploy started: canary/serializer-fix -> eng-runtime-canary-2 (tag: fix/json-stream-escape).

tom_eng: thanks, i'll follow up when the canary is healthy. :eyes:

mike_support: closing loop with customer now, will file billing credit request after confirm.
